A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CBSA/CBT work, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V1 explicitly contains only unfinished appendix headings; v3 supplies substantive appendices A–D. This is a documented addition, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original synthetic-data experiments, classification results, attention-map analyses, ADE20K segmentation results and parameter-perturbation tests.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds quantitative zero-shot segmentation, throughput measurements, initialization-rank observations and larger-model compression analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use pooling, cross-attention extraction, representative contraction, contraction broadcast and ISTA blocks. V3 explicitly documents extraction residuals, learnable step sizes and implementation code, but does not establish an implemented redesign. The added sparsity term clarifies the mathematical account of the already-used ISTA module rather than demonstrating a new training loss.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds PASCAL VOC12 validation evaluation for zero-shot foreground, background and boundary segmentation. The synthetic data, ImageNet, CIFAR, Flowers, Pets and ADE20K coverage is retained, making this a focused extension within visual tasks.

E2.justification: The emergent-segmentation comparison expands: v1 Figure 7 compares CBT, CRATE and their hybrid, while v3 Table 5 additionally evaluates ToST-S. The comparator families in the retained classification, ADE20K and pretrained-ViT adaptation experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate best-performing CLS attention maps using IoU for three VOC12 targets, report layer-wise segmentation, and measure training/inference images per second on 512×512 CIFAR-10 images. Table 4 drops the learned-initialization Agent condition and retains pooling. Newly supplied training schedules document existing experiments rather than establish changed budgets or reruns.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends interpretability analyses through quantitative emergent-segmentation and layer-wise tests in Tables 5–6, CBT-B/L compression-coupling plots in Figure 10, and initialization-rank evidence in Appendix A. Conversely, Table 4 removes the learned-versus-pooled Agent initialization accuracy ablation. The original parameter-perturbation tests remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The Gaussian standard deviation in Figure 8 remains a perturbation setting, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 5–7 add substantial results, including hybrid foreground IoU of 0.68 and CBT-T throughput of 336 training/572 inference images per second. Appendix A adds ranks around 5 versus 64, and Figure 10 adds larger-model curves. Table 3 and retained Table 4 scores are unchanged: Agent scores 62.7/70.6 are removed, while existing pooling scores 63.8/71.8 remain, rather than representing improvements.

T1.justification: V3 adds an explicit sparsity penalty to the objectives and changes Equation 3's initial summed coding-rate equality into per-subspace equalities. Appendix B supplies previously absent derivations of the linear-attention form and its extension to rotated/scaled orthogonal representatives, Equations 14–23. Equation 8 also newly omits the head aggregation and output-projection factors present in v1, creating an apparent inconsistency.

C1.justification: Both versions claim optimization-derived interpretable attention, linear complexity with a fixed representative count, connections to softmax/linear/channel attention, and competitive visual-task performance. V3's emphasis on a 'unified formula' restates the existing central contribution rather than materially changing its scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds modality limitations of linear-subspace modeling, discusses the remaining rank bottleneck under pooling, and qualifies the coding-rate/accuracy correlation as absent after normalization. It also proposes links to in-context learning and superposition. Its new claim of consistently superior throughput is too broad: Table 7 reports faster ToST-S inference than CBT-S.

D1.justification: The previously empty appendix is replaced with concrete reproducibility information: 150-epoch Lion training, learning rates, weight decay, batch sizes, warmup, augmentation, label smoothing and AdamW fine-tuning. Appendix D adds PyTorch code specifying pooling, projections and learnable step sizes. The abstract's code-link destination is unchanged; these additions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V3 broadens positioning through denoising, matrix-decomposition and contrastive-learning interpretations, representative-selection research and algorithm-unrolling foundations. Section 3.3 adds explicit comparisons with Native Hybrid Attention and Log-linear Attention. Section 5 removes the earlier discussion citing Set Transformer, Linformer, Pyramid Vision Transformer and DynamicViT, while adding Performer-related context.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, experimental discussion, related work and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. MCR2 exposition moves into the preliminaries, which gain labeled subsections, and attention variants are reordered under a unified-formula narrative. Broken citation wording is repaired, and affiliation and funding information are expanded.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned with a revised computational diagram and new compression-geometry panels. Figure 3 is relocated and relabeled, Figure 2 is reduced in size, and multiple captions change. V3 adds Tables 5–7, Figure 10 and Algorithm 1, while simplifying Table 4's Agent entries. Most existing empirical plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v1's explicitly unfinished appendix by supplying derivations, training recipes and implementation code, substantially improving inspectability and reproducibility. Quantitative segmentation analyses and measured throughput strengthen evidence beyond v1's attention-map examples and FLOP comparisons. These gains outweigh the removed initialization ablation and localized regressions, including Equation 8's missing factors and the overstated throughput claim: CBT-S inference is 405 images/sec versus ToST-S's 429.
